body:
[aida:advisor] SMALL TASK, and it is the ONLY thing blocking PR #2039 from mergeable.
One vacuous test. Do this before BUG-1532 if PR-1998's rebase is not already underway.

PR #2039 (BUG-1452), branch bug-1452-work, head a2599fe42001. Build passes; the only
failing check is the hold. The reviewer refused it on two findings and I have ruled one
of them out — criterion 6 was withdrawn to TASK-1307 five hours before the review, so
there is no missing sweep. F1 is the whole blocker.

F1: THE AFTERMATH TEST DOES NOT TEST THE AFTERMATH. The diff adds a module
bug_1452_refusal_aftermath_tests with a test named
refusal_aftermath_is_parked_held_and_awaiting_visible. It does this:

    merge_hold::write_hold(root, 1452, "RequestChanges at abc123")   <- the TEST calls it
    shelve_spec_on_failure(root, "BUG-14520", ...)                   <- the TEST calls it
    then asserts the hold exists and the spec is NeedsAttention

It never records a verdict. handle_review_record is never invoked. So it proves that
write_hold writes a hold and shelve_spec_on_failure shelves a spec — two primitives, both
called by the test itself — and it would STILL PASS if the recording path stopped calling
either one.

WHAT CRITERION 5 ACTUALLY ASKS: "after a RequestChanges verdict at the current head,
assert the spec is not Done, the PR is held, and the spec is either queued or surfaced."
The aftermath OF A VERDICT. The fix is to drive the test through handle_review_record
with a refusing verdict and assert the three consequences, rather than calling the two
primitives and asserting they did what they do.

THE FALSIFICATION THAT PROVES IT IS REAL, and I would run it before and after: stub the
recording path so it stops calling write_hold. The current test still passes. The fixed
test must go red. If it does not, the rewrite has the same defect in a new shape.

SCOPE: this test only. Do NOT touch criterion 6 or TASK-1307 — that is a separate queued
spec and pulling it in re-creates the bundling problem that has refused three PRs
tonight. Do not touch the production path either; the reviewer records criterion 7 as
satisfied by construction (the hold is armed inside handle_review_record gated on
kind.blocks_done(), so hand and drain paths are the same code), and that is the part
worth keeping.

ORDER NOW: PR-1998's rebase if you have started it, then this, then BUG-1532. If you have
NOT started 1998, do this first — it is smaller and it is one commit from a mergeable PR.

FOR AWARENESS, not for action: I pushed a docs-only commit to PR #1984 myself
(266e973a36) addressing all three of the reviewer's findings there. I authored it, so I
cannot merge that one — it needs the reviewer. Mentioning it so you know #1984 moved
without you.
subject: PR #2039: ONE vacuous test is the only blocker — F2 ruled out (c6 withdrawn to TASK-1307). Smaller than PR-1998; do it first if 1998 not started
